prs.author: Genmin

prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Streamable HTTP JSON response mode rejects valid requests with a 406 because the Accept-header validation hard-requires both `application/json` and `text/event-stream`, even though JSON response mode never uses SSE. Both PRs relax this check so an `Accept: application/json`-only request is accepted. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: Both patches touch the exact same validation block in webStandardStreamableHttp.ts and ship the same changeset scope. #1996 replaces the check with a spec-aware `acceptsMediaType()` helper that splits the Accept header per RFC 7231 media-range syntax, honors `q=0` (explicitly-unacceptable) parameters, and matches type/subtype including wildcards. #2046 instead does a plain `.includes('application/json')` substring check, which will false-positive on related-but-distinct media types (e.g. `application/json-patch+json`, `application/jsonx`) and ignores quality-value exclusions like `application/json;q=0`. #1996's approach is the more correct, general fix for the same bug, so it should be kept and #2046 closed as a duplicate.

clusters.pick_reason: Both patches touch the exact same validation block in webStandardStreamableHttp.ts and ship the same changeset scope. #1996 replaces the check with a spec-aware `acceptsMediaType()` helper that splits the Accept header per RFC 7231 media-range syntax, honors `q=0` (explicitly-unacceptable) parameters, and matches type/subtype including wildcards. #2046 instead does a plain `.includes('application/json')` substring check, which will false-positive on related-but-distinct media types (e.g. `application/json-patch+json`, `application/jsonx`) and ignores quality-value exclusions like `application/json;q=0`. #1996's approach is the more correct, general fix for the same bug, so it should be kept and #2046 closed as a duplicate.

clusters.pick_reason: Both patches touch the exact same validation block in webStandardStreamableHttp.ts and ship the same changeset scope. #1996 replaces the check with a spec-aware `acceptsMediaType()` helper that splits the Accept header per RFC 7231 media-range syntax, honors `q=0` (explicitly-unacceptable) parameters, and matches type/subtype including wildcards. #2046 instead does a plain `.includes('application/json')` substring check, which will false-positive on related-but-distinct media types (e.g. `application/json-patch+json`, `application/jsonx`) and ignores quality-value exclusions like `application/json;q=0`. #1996's approach is the more correct, general fix for the same bug, so it should be kept and #2046 closed as a duplicate.
